plan.title: Confounded treated vs control lung DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The 12-sample lung bulk RNA-seq dataset (12000 genes x 12 samples, raw salmon gene counts) has batch perfectly confounded with condition: all 6 controls are batch B1, all 6 treated are batch B2. A batch term cannot be added to the model (the design matrix would not be full rank) and no batch-correction method (ComBat-seq, SVA, removeBatchEffect) can be applied without risking removal of the condition effect itself, since batch and condition are identical partitions of the samples. The plan therefore: (1) runs sample-structure QC to show, transparently, that PC1 separates by both batch and condition simultaneously; (2) runs DESeq2 (Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, independent filtering, BH FDR) with design ~condition only, treating the 'condition' effect as an unavoidable composite of true treatment effect and processing-batch effect; (3) runs edgeR quasi-likelihood as an orthogonal method for a robustness check via the DESeq2/edgeR overlap; (4) runs preranked GSEA (fgsea) against Hallmark and Reactome human gene sets, ranking on the Wald statistic, to give a lower-resolution but still informative summary that is less sensitive to single-gene batch artifacts; (5) integrates everything into a report that states the confound explicitly at every level, per the standing rule that a perfectly confounded batch/condition design must be labeled as confounded rather than silently corrected or silently ignored. No result from this analysis can be attributed uniquely to 'treatment' as opposed to 'processing batch' — every step's output is labeled accordingly.
